data.name: Fahreedah
data.gender_notes: Fahreedah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A woman who is free in her actions and thoughts. The name Fahreedah carries the meaning “Free, liberated” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Fahreedah usually hope their child will grow to embody free, liberated and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a woman who is free from the bondages of her past, seeking to live a life in the present moment
data.etymology: Fahreedah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Free, liberated.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fahreedah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: فريدة
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مؤنث يعني الفريد أو الوحيد أو العزيز
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم فريدة مشتق من الفرد الذي يعني الوحيد أو الفريد، ويدل على التفرد والتميز، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة يس آية 11: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَعْطَاكَ فَإِنَّهُ لَفَضْلِهِ وَشُكْرِهِ أَمَلُ الثَّاقِبِينَ ﴾، وله دلالة على الفضل والعزة

in_urdu.name: فریدة
in_urdu.meaning: وہ جو منفرد ہے، عزیز، پیارا، فری
in_urdu.long_meaning: فریدة کا مطلب ہے جو فری ہے یا منفرد ہے، یہ نام عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے فريد، اور یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں بہت اہمیت رکھتا ہے، اور یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے درمیان میں بھی مقبول ہے

in_hindi.name: फ़रीदा

in_pashto.name: فريده

in_english.name: Fahreedah
in_english.long_meaning: Fahreedah is derived from the Arabic root 'ف-ر-د' which means 'to be alone' or 'unique'. The name signifies singularity, uniqueness, and preciousness. It has Quranic roots and historical significance in Islamic tradition. Fahreedah symbolizes a person who is distinct, cherished, and esteemed.
